children: Long-term Japanese government bonds (JGBs) extended gains on Wednesday on signs that safe-haven demand and high yields were bringing investors back to debt markets.
The yield on the 20-year JGB (JP20YTN=JBTC) fell 1 basis point to 3.690%, heading for a third straight session of decline. Yields move inversely to bond prices

Overseas, longer-dated US Treasury yields fell on Tuesday after weak housing data, while German Bund yields dropped on safe-haven demand. The moves came after a broad global selloff over the past month pushed long-end yields to multi-decade highs on inflation risks and heavy government borrowing
JGB yields fell sharply and the yen rallied on Tuesday after an auction of 20-year JGBs saw record-high demand

"The higher yield backdrop is bringing investors back, and in Japan, that result is consistent with signs of increased Japanese capital repatriation," Skye Masters, head of markets research at National Australia Bank, said on a podcast

A Reuters poll published on Wednesday found a majority of economists expect the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise its policy rate to 1.50% in December from 1.25%, with a hike unlikely at the meeting ending October 30
Other JGB tenors had yet to trade early in the session
